prompt: Merchant can view their key monthly metrics and refresh them manually from a clean admin dashboard.

intent.desiredOutcome: Merchant can view their key monthly metrics and refresh them manually from a clean admin dashboard.
intent.qualityBrief: A good version calculates metrics accurately (revenue excluding refunds, AOV from completed orders, repeat customers by email match), renders charts that are legible at a glance, and handles edge cases like no orders in the month or single-order customers gracefully. The Refresh button should provide clear feedback (loading state, timestamp of last refresh). Avoid cluttering the page — four metrics, four simple visualizations, minimal chrome.

plan.dataFlow: A merchant opens the admin dashboard and the page calls the read-metrics-snapshot route, optionally with a month_year, which returns the stored snapshot for that month (defaulting to the current calendar month) along with its timestamp and any in-progress flag. When the merchant clicks Refresh, the admin panel calls the refresh route, which sets the in-progress flag, acquires a per-shop advisory lock so no concurrent refresh can race ahead, fetches all current-month orders from the external system page by page until no further pages remain, hands the full order set to the compute step to derive revenue, AOV, order count, and repeat-customer count, then upserts the result into the snapshot table (clearing the in-progress flag as part of that upsert). If the fetch or compute step throws, the route invokes clear-refresh-in-progress to release the flag without overwriting the previously stored metric values. The admin panel polls the read route during refresh to show the loading state, and on completion renders the updated metrics and the new timestamp.

capabilities.description: Retrieves the stored metrics snapshot for the current calendar month so the dashboard can render without triggering a live computation.

Fetches all orders placed in the current calendar month from the external commerce platform, following cursor-based pagination through every page until no next-page cursor is returned, so the full order set is available before any metric is computed — months with more than one page of results are handled correctly and never silently truncated.

Derives the four key metrics — net revenue excluding refunds, average order value across completed orders, total completed order count, and repeat customer count (defined as customers whose email appears on more than one completed order placed within the current calendar month only; cross-month repeats are out of scope to keep the snapshot self-contained per month) — from the full in-memory order set.

Upserts the computed metrics into the snapshot table for the current calendar month, records the computation timestamp, and clears the in-progress flag; this write must be preceded by acquiring a per-shop advisory lock so that only one refresh computation can reach this upsert at a time.
Marks the current-month snapshot row as refresh-in-progress so the admin UI can display a loading state immediately after the merchant clicks Refresh.

Clears the refresh-in-progress flag without modifying the previously stored metric values; called when the order fetch or compute step fails so the snapshot row does not remain stuck in the in-progress state forever.

persistence.name: metrics_snapshot
persistence.purpose: Stores the most recently computed monthly metrics for each calendar month so the dashboard can render instantly without a live query.

columns.name: snapshot_month
columns.purpose: First day of the calendar month this snapshot covers

columns.name: revenue
columns.purpose: Net revenue for the month excluding refunds

columns.name: average_order_value
columns.purpose: Mean order value across completed orders for the month

columns.name: order_count
columns.purpose: Number of completed orders in the month

columns.name: repeat_customer_count
columns.purpose: Number of customers whose email appears on more than one completed order within this snapshot's calendar month (intra-month repeats only; cross-month repeats are not counted)

columns.name: computed_at
columns.purpose: Wall-clock time when the last successful computation completed

columns.name: refresh_in_progress
columns.purpose: Indicates a refresh computation is currently running for this month

persistence.keyedBy: one row per calendar month, keyed by the first day of that month
queryPatterns: single row lookup by calendar month for the dashboard read
single row upsert by calendar month on refresh completion

externalContracts.purpose: Returns the stored metrics snapshot for a calendar month, including all four metric values, the last-computed timestamp, and the in-progress flag so the UI can render the correct initial state. Defaults to the server's current calendar month when no month_year is supplied; when a month_year is supplied the snapshot for that historical month is returned, and if no row exists for that month the server returns null metric values with computed_at null and refresh_in_progress false so the UI can render an empty state.

Initiates a full recomputation of the current-month metrics from live order data; immediately sets the in-progress flag and returns so the UI can begin showing the loading state while computation proceeds.

edgeCases: The current month has no completed orders — all four metrics must be recorded as zero rather than null so the dashboard renders empty-state visualizations instead of blank or broken charts.
All orders in the month were fully refunded — net revenue must be zero and AOV must be computed only over completed non-zero orders, not produce a divide-by-zero error.
Every customer in the month placed exactly one order — repeat customer count must be recorded as zero and the visualization must render a graceful empty state rather than omitting the metric.

A refresh is triggered while a previous refresh for the same shop is still in flight — the system must enforce a per-shop advisory lock so only one computation runs at a time; the second request must either wait for the lock and then return the in-progress status, or return the in-progress status immediately, preventing a race condition where both computations reach the upsert and the snapshot reflects whichever commit arrived last.

The external system returns an error or times out mid-pagination — the refresh must be rolled back via clear-refresh-in-progress, the in-progress flag must be cleared without touching the previously stored metric values, and the previously stored snapshot must remain intact so the dashboard does not display partial or empty metrics; without this explicit clear capability the row would remain stuck in refresh_in_progress=true and block all future Refresh attempts.

The merchant's clock-local month boundary differs from UTC — the system must consistently define the month boundary in a single reference timezone applied uniformly to both the fetch filter and the snapshot key to avoid orders near midnight on month boundaries being double-counted or dropped.

hld_v_findings.issue: The capability reads all orders for the current calendar month from the Shopify Admin API but describes no pagination loop. Shopify returns at most 250 orders per page, so any month with more than 250 orders will silently produce metrics computed on a truncated dataset — revenue, AOV, and repeat-customer count will all be understated with no error surfaced.
hld_v_findings.fix: Add a dataNeeds entry for 'pagination cursor / page_info' and document in the capability description that the implementation must follow Shopify's cursor-based pagination until no next-page token is returned before handing the full order set to compute-monthly-metrics.

hld_v_findings.issue: The edge case claims concurrent refreshes are 'processed sequentially', but no serialization primitive (database advisory lock, queue, or idempotency key) is defined anywhere in the plan to enforce this. Without a mechanism, two concurrent POST requests will both read order data, both compute, and race on the upsert — the snapshot may reflect the earlier computation depending on commit order, contradicting the stated guarantee.
hld_v_findings.fix: Add an edge case (or a note in save-metrics-snapshot) specifying a per-shop advisory lock or a queued-job pattern so only one refresh computation runs at a time, with the second request either waiting or returning the in-progress result.

hld_v_findings.issue: The route always returns the current calendar month with no month_year query parameter in the requestShape, making it impossible for the admin UI to display or compare a prior month's snapshot without introducing a new endpoint or a breaking change to this one.
hld_v_findings.fix: Add an optional 'month_year' field to the requestShape (defaulting to the server's current month when absent) so the same endpoint can serve historical snapshots already stored in monthly_metrics_snapshot.

hld_v_findings.issue: The response shape includes a 'has_data' flag, implying a no-snapshot state (e.g., first load at the start of a new month) is anticipated, but no edge case describes what values the other fields carry when has_data is false — null, zero, or omitted — leaving the front-end rendering logic undefined for this scenario.
hld_v_findings.fix: Add an edge case stating that when no snapshot row exists for the current month, the GET returns has_data: false with all numeric fields as zero and refreshed_at as null, so the UI knows to prompt the merchant to run the first Refresh.

hld_v_findings.issue: The plan defines 'repeat customer count' as customers with more than one order within the current month only, but the quality brief describes 'repeat customers by email match' without a same-month restriction; a merchant may reasonably expect cross-month repeat customers, and the narrower definition will silently undercount in low-volume months.
hld_v_findings.fix: Explicitly document in the compute-monthly-metrics description and the column purpose that repeat-customer scope is intentionally limited to the current calendar month, so LLD implementers do not expand it and product stakeholders can confirm the interpretation.
